This page demonstrates the **Quarto Semantic Components** extension. In each section, the source code appears **before** the rendered output.

## Project defaults in `_quarto.yml`

This repository uses shared defaults:

```yaml
extensions:
  badge:
    - key: stable
      label: Stable
      type: success
      appearance: solid
      icon: "✓"
    - key: experimental
      label: Experimental
      type: info
      appearance: outline
      icon: "⚗"
    - key: deprecated
      label: Deprecated
      type: danger
      appearance: soft
      icon: "!"

  steps:
    dot-color: "#8c959f"
    dot-size: "0.72rem"
    line-color: "#9aa0a6"
    line-width: "1.5px"

  file-tree:
    icons: devicon
    expanded: true
    indent: "1.8rem"

  git-tree:
    direction: TB
    line-color: "#9aa0a6"
    line-width: "2px"
    node-size: "0.68rem"
    lane-gap: "0.82rem"
    row-height: "36px"
    content-gap: "0.55rem"

  article:
    radius: "0.75rem"
    padding: "1rem 1.1rem"
    accent: none
```

Precedence is **project defaults → preset → component → individual item**.

## Badges inline

> The public shortcode is `badge`. Since [`mcanouil/quarto-badge`](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-badge) uses the same name, the project must choose which badge extension to use.

### Presets defined in the project

```{.markdown shortcodes=false}
{{< badge stable >}}
{{< badge experimental >}}
{{< badge deprecated >}}
{{< badge "Stable release" key="stable" >}}
```

**Output:**

{{< badge stable >}} {{< badge experimental >}} {{< badge deprecated >}} {{< badge "Stable release" key="stable" >}}

### Free customization

```{.markdown shortcodes=false}
{{< badge "Beta" >}}
{{< badge "Stable" type="success" icon="✓" >}}
{{< badge "Experimental" type="warning" appearance="outline" >}}
{{< badge "v0.10.9" type="accent" appearance="solid" >}}
```

**Output:**

{{< badge "Beta" >}} {{< badge "Stable" type="success" icon="✓" >}} {{< badge "Experimental" type="warning" appearance="outline" >}} {{< badge "v0.10.9" type="accent" appearance="solid" >}}

### Forma AST-native

```markdown
[AST-native]{.badge key="stable" appearance="outline" size="md"}
```

**Output:** [AST-native]{.badge key="stable" appearance="outline" size="md"}

## Steps — numerado

All `steps` examples use four steps. In numbered mode, the edge is also continuous between circle centers and stays behind the markers; the inside follows the theme surface.

```markdown
:::steps
## Install the extension
Use `quarto add lsbjordao/quarto-semantic-components`.

## Enable the filter
Add `semantic-components` to `filters`.

## Configure the components
Set defaults in `_quarto.yml` if desired.

## Write normally
Each heading starts a step.
:::
```

**Output:**

:::steps
## Install the extension
Use `quarto add lsbjordao/quarto-semantic-components`.

## Enable the filter
Add `semantic-components` to `filters`.

## Configure the components
Set defaults in `_quarto.yml` if desired.

## Write normally
Each heading starts a step.
:::

## Steps — dots

Dots look hollow by default: the center uses the theme surface color, hiding the continuous edge that passes behind them. `dot-color` controls the outline and `dot-fill` enables explicit fill.

### Project default

```markdown
::: {.steps type="dots"}
## Extract
Download the data.

## Validate
Validate the records.

## Transform
Prepare the data.

## Publish
Publish the result.
:::
```

**Output:**

::: {.steps type="dots"}
## Extract
Download the data.

## Validate
Validate the records.

## Transform
Prepare the data.

## Publish
Publish the result.
:::

### Custom background

If the steps sit on a surface different from the document background, use `surface-color` so the dot centers match that background:

```markdown
::: {.steps type="dots"
  surface-color="#f3f4f6"
  line-color="#9aa0a6"}

## Prepare
First step.

## Process
Second step.

## Review
Third step.

## Publish
Fourth step.

:::
```

### Dot color and size

```markdown
::: {.steps type="dots"
  dot-color="#8c959f"
  dot-size="0.78rem"
  line-color="#9aa0a6"
  line-width="1.5px"}

## Extract {dot-color="#2563eb"}
Download the new records.

## Deduplicate {dot-color="#f59e0b" dot-size="0.95rem"}
Reconcile collections and identifications.

## Review {dot-color="#8b5cf6"}
Review the processed dataset.

## Publish {dot-color="#16a34a"}
Update the curated dataset.
:::
```

**Output:**

::: {.steps type="dots" dot-color="#8c959f" dot-size="0.78rem" line-color="#9aa0a6" line-width="1.5px"}
## Extract {dot-color="#2563eb"}
Download the new records.

## Deduplicate {dot-color="#f59e0b" dot-size="0.95rem"}
Reconcile collections and identifications.

## Review {dot-color="#8b5cf6"}
Review the processed dataset.

## Publish {dot-color="#16a34a"}
Update the curated dataset.
:::

### Optional fill

```markdown
::: {.steps type="dots" line-width="2px"}
## Pending
Remains hollow.

## In progress {dot-color="#2563eb" dot-fill="#2563eb"}
Filled blue dot.

## Under review {dot-color="#f59e0b" dot-fill="#f59e0b"}
Filled orange dot.

## Completed {dot-color="#16a34a" dot-fill="#16a34a" dot-border-width="2px"}
Filled green dot.
:::
```

**Output:**

::: {.steps type="dots" line-width="2px"}
## Pending
Remains hollow.

## In progress {dot-color="#2563eb" dot-fill="#2563eb"}
Filled blue dot.

## Under review {dot-color="#f59e0b" dot-fill="#f59e0b"}
Filled orange dot.

## Completed {dot-color="#16a34a" dot-fill="#16a34a" dot-border-width="2px"}
Filled green dot.
:::

### Example — timeline with Steps dots

There is no separate `timeline` component. The same visual pattern is produced with `steps type="dots"`, keeping the API smaller and more reusable.

```markdown
::: {.steps type="dots"
  line-color="#9aa0a6"
  line-width="2px"
  dot-size="0.78rem"}

## [2024]{.badge type="success" appearance="outline" size="xs"} Prototype {dot-color="#16a34a"}
First implementation of the component.

## [2025]{.badge type="info" appearance="outline" size="xs"} Beta {dot-color="#2563eb"}
Validation and visual refinement.

## [2026-06]{.badge type="warning" appearance="outline" size="xs"} Release candidate {dot-color="#f59e0b"}
API freeze for final testing.

## [2026-09]{.badge type="success" appearance="solid" size="xs"} Release {dot-color="#16a34a"}
Stable version released.

:::
```

**Output:**

::: {.steps type="dots" line-color="#9aa0a6" line-width="2px" dot-size="0.78rem"}

## [2024]{.badge type="success" appearance="outline" size="xs"} Prototype {dot-color="#16a34a"}
First implementation of the component.

## [2025]{.badge type="info" appearance="outline" size="xs"} Beta {dot-color="#2563eb"}
Validation and visual refinement.

## [2026-06]{.badge type="warning" appearance="outline" size="xs"} Release candidate {dot-color="#f59e0b"}
API freeze for final testing.

## [2026-09]{.badge type="success" appearance="solid" size="xs"} Release {dot-color="#16a34a"}
Stable version released.

:::

## Git tree — DAG de commits

The graph represents commits and parent → child relationships. Branches split from nodes; merges end at nodes; the tag and description follow the commit lane.

### Simple syntax — TB direction

```markdown
::: {.git-tree direction="TB"}
- `main` initial commit
- `main` creates the base architecture
  - `feature/icons` opens the icons branch
  - `feature/icons` adds Devicon
    - `docs/icons` documents providers
    - `docs/icons` adds examples
  - `feature/icons` merge docs/icons
  - `feature/icons` adds file links
- `main` merge feature/icons
- `main` starts inline components
  - `feature/badges` creates badge
  - `feature/badges` adds visual customization
    - `test/badges` covers variants
    - `test/badges` covers links
  - `feature/badges` merge test/badges
- `main` merge feature/badges
- `main` release v0.10.9
:::
```

**Output:**

::: {.git-tree direction="TB"}
- `main` initial commit
- `main` creates the base architecture
  - `feature/icons` opens the icons branch
  - `feature/icons` adds Devicon
    - `docs/icons` documents providers
    - `docs/icons` adds examples
  - `feature/icons` merge docs/icons
  - `feature/icons` adds file links
- `main` merge feature/icons
- `main` starts inline components
  - `feature/badges` creates badge
  - `feature/badges` adds visual customization
    - `test/badges` covers variants
    - `test/badges` covers links
  - `feature/badges` merge test/badges
- `main` merge feature/badges
- `main` release v0.10.9
:::

### Same DAG — BT direction

```markdown
::: {.git-tree direction="BT"}
- `main` initial commit
- `main` base architecture
  - `feature/api` creates API
  - `feature/api` implementa endpoints
- `main` merge feature/api
- `main` release
:::
```

**Output:**

::: {.git-tree direction="BT"}
- `main` initial commit
- `main` base architecture
  - `feature/api` creates API
  - `feature/api` implementa endpoints
- `main` merge feature/api
- `main` release
:::

### Explicit DAG — ids, parents, tag, and HEAD

```markdown
:::git-tree
- `main`{#c1} initial commit
- `main`{#c2 parent="c1"} base architecture
  - `feature/badges`{#c3 parent="c2"} creates badge
  - `feature/badges`{#c4 parent="c3"} visual customization
    - `test/badges`{#c5 parent="c4"} covers variants
    - `test/badges`{#c6 parent="c5"} covers links
  - `feature/badges`{#c7 parents="c4,c6"} merge test/badges
- `main`{#c8 parents="c2,c7" tag="v0.10.9" head="true"} merge feature/badges
:::
```

**Output:**

:::git-tree
- `main`{#c1} initial commit
- `main`{#c2 parent="c1"} base architecture
  - `feature/badges`{#c3 parent="c2"} creates badge
  - `feature/badges`{#c4 parent="c3"} visual customization
    - `test/badges`{#c5 parent="c4"} covers variants
    - `test/badges`{#c6 parent="c5"} covers links
  - `feature/badges`{#c7 parents="c4,c6"} merge test/badges
- `main`{#c8 parents="c2,c7" tag="v0.10.9" head="true"} merge feature/badges
:::

## File tree — deep nesting and icons

```markdown

- +project
  - +src
    - +pipelines
      - +python
        - pipeline.py ingestion
        - validate.py validation
      - +r
        - analysis.R statistical analysis
        - report.Rmd report
      - +web
        - +src
          - +components
            - chart.ts
            - table.ts
          - app.ts
    - +database
      - +migrations
        - schema.sql
  - +docs
    - report.qmd
  - +data
    - +processed
      - occurrences.parquet
  - README.md
  - _quarto.yml
:::
```

- +project
  - +src

## File tree — horizontal indentation

The per-level indentation can be changed with `indent`. This gallery defaults to `1.8rem`.

```markdown
::: {.file-tree indent="1rem"}
- +src
  - +components
    - Button.ts
    - Card.ts
  - app.ts
- +database
  - schema.sql
:::
```

**Output:**

::: {.file-tree indent="1rem"}
- +src
  - +components
    - Button.ts
    - Card.ts
  - app.ts
- +database
  - schema.sql
:::

Use larger values, such as `indent="2.4rem"`, to spread the hierarchy out more visually.

## File tree — expand and collapse folders

::: {.file-tree expanded="false"}
- [+src]{expanded="true"}

## Article

`article` is the generic primitive for self-contained content. The outer HTML element is always `<article>`.

### Generic — rounded border only

```markdown
:::article
## Technical note
This is the default `article`, with no accent and no collapse.
:::
```

**Output:**

:::article
## Technical note
This is the default `article`, with no accent and no collapse.
:::

### Left accent with rounded ends

```markdown
::: {.article accent="left" accent-color="warning"}
## Attention
The side accent is optional. The component remains an `article`.
:::
```

**Output:**

::: {.article accent="left" accent-color="warning"}
## Attention
The side accent is optional. The component remains an `article`.
:::

Use `accent-color="warning"`, `note`, `danger`, `success`, `important`, or any CSS color such as `#8b5cf6`. `accent-width` controls the thickness.

### Collapsed by default

```markdown
::: {.article
  collapsible="true"
  summary="Technical details"
  expanded="false"}

The content is inside a native `details`, while the outer element remains `article`.

- Markdown normal
- listas
- code
- outros componentes

:::
```

**Output:**

::: {.article collapsible="true" summary="Technical details" expanded="false"}

The content is inside a native `details`, while the outer element remains `article`.

- Markdown normal
- listas
- code
- outros componentes

:::

### Expanded + accent

```markdown
::: {.article
  accent="left"
  accent-color="note"
  collapsible="true"
  summary="Metodologia"
  expanded="true"}

This example starts expanded and combines accent with collapse.

:::
```

**Output:**

::: {.article accent="left" accent-color="note" collapsible="true" summary="Metodologia" expanded="true"}

This example starts expanded and combines accent with collapse.

:::

### Example — changelog inside an article

```markdown
:::article

## 0.10.9 — 2026-09-17

### Added
- Optional left accent in `article`.
- Collapse/expand nativo.

### Changed
- Timeline demonstrada com `steps type="dots"`.
- Generic blocks converged on `article`.

### Removed
- `timeline`
- `pipeline`
- `details`
- `changelog`
- `aside`

## 0.7.1 — 2026-09-17

### Changed
- New `content-gap` in `git-tree`.
- Tags and descriptions follow the commit lane.

:::
```

**Output:**

:::article

## 0.10.9 — 2026-09-17

### Added
- Optional left accent in `article`.
- Collapse/expand nativo.

### Changed
- Timeline demonstrada com `steps type="dots"`.
- Generic blocks converged on `article`.

### Removed
- `timeline`
- `pipeline`
- `details`
- `changelog`
- `aside`

## 0.7.1 — 2026-09-17

### Changed
- New `content-gap` in `git-tree`.
- Tags and descriptions follow the commit lane.

:::

### Custom article

```markdown
::: {.article
  radius="1.2rem"
  padding="1.25rem"
  border-color="#8b5cf6"
  background="transparent"}

## Self-contained content
An `article` can also represent posts, releases, summaries, or specifications.
:::
```

**Output:**

::: {.article radius="1.2rem" padding="1.25rem" border-color="#8b5cf6" background="transparent"}
## Self-contained content
An `article` can also represent posts, releases, summaries, or specifications.
:::


## Inspiration and formats

The **Steps** and **File Tree** ideas were inspired by [Vocs](https://vocs.dev/) components, but the implementation is original and Pandoc-AST-oriented.

- **HTML**: full presentation, badges, interactive file tree, info, Git DAG in SVG, and the semantic `article` element;
- **PDF**: structural content and links are preserved;
- **DOCX**: lists, headings, links, and text remain editable.
